item.content:encoded: Is it just me or is the test log for this one rather redundant and blase? I feel like the description is perfectly adequate at conveying the status of test subjects entering the building, and the test log should only be present if there are more in depth logs including dialogue or described film (possibly up the creep factor via language and test subjects pleading to leave the facility and get water and shade from an unseeable sun).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love it and I'm upvoting but I feel that there are some stylistic issues:

1. Addenda could go into a seperate experiment log
2.

Recognizable apparitions appear to be individuals who have been exposed to SCP-358 beyond the average (47 minute) psychological recoverability point in the past.

In my mind this means that anyone who has had untreatable psychological effects becomes an
apparition; I think it could be clarified by saying something like 'Recognizable apparitions appear to be individuals who have experienced untreatable psychological effects in the past'. Otherwise it seems like there is an exact cutoff of 47 minutes that leads to insanity which kind of diminishes the creepiness in my opinion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: 'They' would work (also hey not everyone who identifies as 'male' uses he/him pronouns so there's always that to consider). By Foundation standards, I would probably use 'it' as the Foundation tends to consider SCPs as objects, not as people. I believe it is advised in the 'how to write an SCP' to use 'it' for humanoids due to this reason?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think "they" is generally accepted these days as okay to use for an individual when you're not wanting to specify, but also sort of works better in these contexts because "they" removes humanity from the test subject a little bit. We can force non-human things to go through all these terrible experiments we come up with, but wouldn't dream of inflicting such things on another person. =P

item.content:encoded: Euclid makes more sense for me. True, it doesn't hurt anyone if they just don't go inside, but it doesn't pass the locked box test. It's a building that someone who really wants to sneak inside can, and requires patrols to make sure no one's trying to do so, etc. I imagine there's some sort of misinformation campaign around the building as well. "It's, umm… structurally unsound… yeah… and it's, umm… totally on top of a sinkhole thing too, so building something new on the site wouldn't be plausible, either. Yep. That's totally what's going on there." =P

item.content:encoded:
Oh wow, how'd I miss this when I was reading through? Yeah, I think that should be fixed. Like, "subject has been in a persistent vegetative state since retrieval."

As a below comment says, I also don't get why ages and heights are blackboxed. Percentages are okay to blackbox sometimes, but basic features of test subjects? Doesn't make sense to me.

Didn't want to make posts on multiple really old comments, so wanted to add that here instead of down below.

Those two things are keeping me from upvoting right now. Otherwise like the SCP as a whole. It's just… weird, and I sometimes like it when a scip just makes me think "wtf is this and how did it get there?"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Surprised this doesn't have more likes. It's weird, creepy, interesting, and well-written. It has a good central theme.

 Exploration and monitoring has revealed anomalous activity characteristic of typical type three pseudospiritual manifestation (haunting) ranging from glowing spheres to full bodied apparitions, all of which appear exhausted and on occasion ask for water. Recognizable apparitions appear to be individuals who have been exposed to SCP-358 beyond the average (47 minute) psychological recoverability point in the past. The majority of these subjects reside in Foundation psychological observational facilities, and security footage shows them present in their respective units during the appearance of their apparitions within SCP-358.

See, I feel like this is how 'haunted' SCPs should be written. The Foundation probably deals with normal hauntings all the time. OF COURSE they have techno-lingo and classification type numbers for this stuff… this is a slow Tuesday for them. On the other hand, I think this should be "Safe."

Despite that, tentative upvote.

Given the repeated mention of sand in test subjects' shoes, I'd expect to see a note about testing done on it. Perhaps something along the lines of "Testing shows the sand recovered from test subjects' shoes to be composed primarily of silica, with trace mineral and organic components consistent with [REDACTED]"

A couple of pedantic notes - "ER" stands for "Emergency Room", so the photo is apparently of an Emergency Room room; also, at least in American spelling, there is no "u" in "forty", but if that's a proper spelling in another English-speaking country (yay Americans doing things differently) it's all good.
